input.body:
## Summary

```text
local original SWF → authored observer subclass → local probe copy
owned Ruffle browser → native pointer replay → numeric/text target fixture
native picker / release controller / application comparison → separate follow-up
```

Recover repeatable original-input evidence before wiring the new menu picker. Builds on #41, including its state-based fullscreen test correction. No application behavior changes.

## Evidence

- **Before:** native menu target assumptions have no repeatable observer or retained fixture in the landed branch.
  **After:**13 fresh outcomes distinguish inner controls from decorative wrappers, hover-grown edges from idle edges, empty corners and icon-only release. Pressing outside at(400,410), then releasing over Settings at(203.9,299.4), opens Settings and reports `inner settings_btn`.
- Two probe generations are byte-identical, SHA256 cadbdfa5e02efe4c4fc74a5ab8548055691bbd17b06379a4438919161f585ca3. Independent tag inspection finds one added327-byte DoABC body and the document-class binding change;3021 other original tags are byte-identical. No SWF/artwork/media is committed.
- The prior12 semantic observations reproduce. Four startup trace events differ, so raw timing is not claimed identical. Target tracking now clears on mouse-out; raw traces remain stronger evidence than synthesized names. The fixture records original-input and probe hashes.
- The owned Ruffle0.7.1 replay passes. REA passively captured the resulting Settings viewport; Playwright performed input. Formatting, TypeScript,474 rule/parser tests /5990 assertions and production build pass. Viewer URL, CDP endpoint and capture directory are configurable; shared surfaces were untouched and owned processes closed.
- This observer changes root class identity/listener work/timing, logs names rather than object identity, and runs after descendant handlers. Exact Adobe dispatch, global phase, native recreation picking and complete-game parity remain unproven. docs/fidelity.md records scope, provenance and replay usage.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** tooling

Adds developer-only observation tools and a text/numeric fixture. Generated game copies and captures stay local; renderer and pointer integration follow separately.
